bib.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents", Yuxing Lu, Yicheng Chen, Shanchan Wu, Sercan O. Arik (Google; Georgia Tech; Peking U). Preprint, arXiv 2609.09153v1 [cs.AI], 8 Sep 2026. Not peer reviewed.

COVERAGE: 115,401 chars extracted. I read about 80% in full: the abstract through the conclusion, B.1 to B.4, D, E and Table 11. I skimmed or skipped the rest:
- Appendix A (related-work comparison of 24 methods), B.5 (prompt templates), B.6 (algorithm), C (EnterpriseArena mechanics and case study, though Table 8 numbers are not read) and F (execution cases). I read none of these in full.
- The reference list.
- One image stream failed to decode ("Impossible to decode XFormObject /Im4"); the text is otherwise clean.

NOTE PLACEMENT: notes/ has no "12-*" with this topic. Note 12 is 12-kg-as-shared-agent-memory.md, and this paper is not about shared KG memory. Better fits: 05-topology-patterns.md (explicit editable procedure graph steering an agent), 01-graph-vs-loop.md (graph vs free ReAct loop), or 07-failure-modes-at-scale.md (tool-order errors, repeated actions, drift). It is only loosely related to 12, through the KG analogy and "knowledge outside weights".

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Procedural Graph (PG) beats six memory baselines under a shared ReAct solver.
 number: first or joint first in 21 of 24 model-benchmark settings; 19 wins, 2 ties, 3 losses vs the strongest baseline; p=4.3e-4
 setup: 6 benchmarks (HotpotQA, MultiChallenge, GDPval, ALFWorld, tau-bench, BFCL v3), 4 LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.1 Fast), temperature 0, h=2 hops, w=3 window. Baselines: MemoryBank, RAP, ExpeL, AutoGuide, AWM, KnowAgent, all trained on the same trajectories.
 quote: "PG ranks first or joint first in 21 of 24 model–benchmark settings. Compared with the strongest baseline in each setting, PG records 19 wins, two ties, and three losses (one-sided exact binomial sign test excluding ties, 𝑝= 4.3× 10−4)."
 where: Sec 5.1, Table 1
 Largest margins: BFCL v3 Gemini 3.5 Flash 67.00 vs 58.00; GDPval Gemini 3.1 Pro 78.78 vs 71.37; tau-bench Gemini 3.1 Pro 80.00 vs 73.04. HotpotQA margins are tiny: quote "margins over the strongest baseline range from−0.90to +1.30points". Table 1 CIs are wide on small test sets (BFCL n=100, GDPval n=44).
2. Localized subgraph plus generative guidance beats raw injection and full-graph guidance.
 number: MultiChallenge 89.31, GDPval 63.99, ALFWorld 81.53 vs no-graph 80.27 / 54.80 / 72.58. Full-graph generative on ALFWorld drops to 54.48.
 setup: Gemini 3.5 Flash only, fixed subsets, same graph
 quote: "Full-graph generative guidance further reduces ALFWorld success to54.48while increasing token consumption." and "Localizationreducestotaltokensrelativetofull-graphgenerativeguidanceonallthreebenchmarks: by70.9%on ALFWorld,18.1%on GDPval, and14.8%on MultiChallenge."
 where: Sec 5.5, Table 3
 Cost: tokens stay above the no-graph baseline. Quote: "total token consumption remains33.4%and55.4%higher" on GDPval and ALFWorld. Solver steps fall 28.20 to 18.57 (GDPval) and 21.84 to 18.80 (ALFWorld).
3. Self-evolution from a bare Start->End skeleton matches or beats hand-built graphs, and repairs a bad expert prior.
 number: MultiChallenge: no graph 87.50, expert graph 58.93, expert + one static update 53.57, expert + gated online evolution 92.86, scratch + online evolution 91.07. HotpotQA scratch + online evolution F1 78.79 / EM 66.30 vs baseline 71.21 / 58.8.
 setup: Gemini 3.5 Flash; MultiChallenge 56-sample fast split; HotpotQA 1,000 test; accept gate uses held-out validation (1,000 HotpotQA, 100 MultiChallenge)
 quote: "Mode 1) lowers success from87.50%to58 .93%. A single offline update (Mode 2) further lowers success to53.57%. The iterative configuration (Mode 3) ... recovers to92.86%, a gain of33.93points over the expert initialization."
 where: Sec 5.3, Table 2, App D.1
 A single ungated static update made things worse. Scratch + static build (Mode 4) on HotpotQA scored 69.49 F1, below baseline 71.21. So the iterative, gated loop matters, not just LLM refinement.
4. Long-horizon resilience on EnterpriseArena (monthly CFO sim, up to 132 months, three undisclosed crises).
 number: full-horizon survival 44.0% to 58.0% (Claude Sonnet 4.6), 6.0% to 34.0% (Gemini 3.1 Pro), 26.0% to 40.0% (Grok 4.1 Fast)
 setup: 50 test episodes; ensemble results across 4 LLMs
 quote: "It raises survival from44.0%to58 .0%for Claude Sonnet 4.6, from6.0%to34 .0%for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and from26.0%to40 .0%for Grok 4.1 Fast"
 where: Sec 5.2, Fig 3, Table 8 (not read)
 Mechanism: anticipatory fundraising, since capital arrives 1 to 6 months after the request. Quote: "Average capital raised is$0.00M for the Flash baseline, compared with$9.39M for PG-guided Flash". Tool calls can fall (Flash 18.94 to 12.53 per month) or rise (Sonnet 0.13 to 0.36; Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.89 to 3.18), so the change is which tools are called and when.
5. Ten-round self-evolution trace.
 number: validation survival 0.0% to 45.0% (round 1) to 80.0% (round 2) to 90.0% (round 8); test survival 85.0% vs baseline 0.0% (Fisher p=2.6e-8); tools per month 17.23 to 3.08 (81.8% cut)
 setup: Gemini 3.5 Flash; only 20 episodes per split in the self-evolution study
 quote: "The returned graph reaches85 .0%test survival against the baseline’s0.0%(Fisher’s exact 𝑝= 2.6× 10−8), while the best single round observed during the search reached95.0%; we report the former, since quoting the latter would amount to selecting on the test set."
 where: Sec 5.4, Table 11, App E.1
 Evolved topology (Fig 5): round 1 found the backbone Start->Month_Start->check_cash->cash_flow_forecast->save_note->check_market->Decide_Capital. Round 2 added recall_notes. Round 7 pruned pass_action. Round 8 added a bypass edge. Rounds 3, 4, 6 and 10 were rolled back by the gate and round 5 failed structural checks; round 10 had training survival 90.0% but validation 85.0%.
6. Graph design facts.
 number: 4 relation types (LEADS_TO, TRIGGERS, PROVIDES_INPUT_FOR, CONVERGES_TO); 3 edge attributes (condition, guidance, pitfalls); 7 to 17 nodes and 7 to 27 triplets per graph, except BFCL v3 with 131 nodes and 265 triplets
 quote: "outside of BFCL v3, whose131nodes mirror its large function catalog, every graph has between7and17nodes and between7and27triplets."
 where: App B.4, Sec 3.1
 Mechanics: the active node is found by exact match on the last action; the 2-hop neighborhood goes to a guidance LLM, which writes guidance appended to the solver prompt. The solver chooses freely ("soft" steering). If matching fails, the full graph is used.
 Evolution loop (Sec 3.3): contrast good and bad traces, then Add/Delete edits (attribute update = delete + re-add), then a validation gate (commit if S_val >= current), then a rejection memory fed back to the refiner.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (conclusion): "Guidance increases token use even when it reduces solver steps". Transfer across solvers and tool interfaces is untested.
- Per-edit accept/reject decisions: "With20episodes per split, individual accept/reject decisions turn on one or two episodes and should be read as a search trace rather than as significance tests."
- Table 2 and ablation studies use one model (Gemini 3.5 Flash) and small splits (MultiChallenge 56, ALFWorld/GDPval subsets). Greedy decoding gives one run per cell; no seed variance. The gate's S_val cache is also noisy under stochastic evaluation, and the paper says it is examined in 5.4.
- HotpotQA gains are within noise. GDPval has only 44 test tasks.
- Judge is Gemini 3.1 Pro, while Gemini models are also among the evaluated solvers.
- The guidance model and refiner always share the solver's LLM. No test of a weak solver with a strong refiner.
- Matching is exact on the last action, so free-text "reasoning" nodes depend on how nodes are defined.
- Expert graph results show a hand-built graph can hurt (58.93 vs 87.50).
- I could not verify the 24-method comparison (App A) or the Table 8 numbers.
- No explicit limitations section found in the extraction.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023b) as the solver; ExpeL (Zhao et al., 2024) for contrasting success and failure; AutoGuide (Fu et al., NeurIPS 2024) for state-conditioned guidelines; Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); AWM (Wang et al., 2025b) for workflows; KnowAgent (Zhu et al., 2025) for action-transition rules; MemoryBank (Zhong et al., 2024); RAP (Kagaya et al., NeurIPS 2024 workshop); Memp (Fang et al., 2025, arXiv 2508.06433); automated workflow search (Zhang et al., 2025); Xiao et al. 2024 (workflow knowledge); tool graph work (Liu et al. 2024a,b; Lumer et al., 2025). Benchmarks: HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018); MultiChallenge (Deshpande et al., ACL Findings 2025); GDPval (Patwardhan et al., 2025); ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021); tau-bench (Yao et al., 2024); BFCL (Patil et al., 2025); EnterpriseArena (Han et al., 2026, arXiv 2603.23638). The knowledge-graph analogy is the framing; GraphRAG (Edge et al., 2024) and Graph of Thoughts (Besta et al., AAAI 2024) are cited.

CODE: none in the paper. Useful formulas (verbatim from Sec 3.2 and 3.3):
- gate: "G𝑘 = Gcand𝑘 if 𝑆val(Gcand𝑘 ) ≥ 𝑆val(G𝑘−1), else G𝑘−1" (Eq. 5)
- solver: "𝑎𝑡∼𝑃solver(· | 𝑞,T𝑡, 𝑔𝑡)" (Eq. 3)
- example edge (Sec 3.1): (cash_flow_forecast, LEADS_TO, fund_raising_request) with condition / guidance / pitfalls text.

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (p.4), "Overview of the Procedural Graph framework." This is the one figure candidate. It shows the online path (localize node, 2-hop subgraph, guidance LLM, solver prompt) beside the offline loop (refiner, validation gate, commit or rollback, rejected memory), so it explains the design faster than prose.
- Others, not chosen: Fig 1 (KG vs PG analogy); Fig 5 (graph topology across evolution rounds, p.34; good for a worked example); Fig 3 (survival curves); Fig 4.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 1 columns run together in the extraction but values are parseable. One PDF image stream failed to decode. Appendix text on 2026-dated models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.1 Fast) is as printed; I did not check it elsewhere. Extracted text is at /tmp/pg.txt (scratch only).
